stem: A die has six faces numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Manjit suspects that the die is biased so that it shows a six on fewer throws than it would if it were fair. In order to test her suspicion, she throws the die a certain number of times and counts the number of sixes.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: State suitable null and alternative hypotheses for Manjit’s test.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: There are no sixes in the first 15 throws. Show that this result is not significant at the 5% level.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Find the smallest value of $n$ such that, if there are no sixes in the first $n$ throws, this result is significant at the 5% level.
